Class MusicPlayerService

java.lang.Object
com.sebastiandorata.musicdashboard.service.MusicPlayerService
@Service @SessionScope public class MusicPlayerService extends Object
Server-side playback state for one logged-in browser session: queue, current song and tracking flags.

The browser plays the audio with an HTML5 Audio element; this service keeps the decisions the desktop MusicPlayerService made around the MediaPlayer: the shuffled queue, wrap-around next/previous, "previous restarts the song after 3 seconds", and the rules that decide when a play is written to the listening history. Wherever the desktop read the media player's current time or total duration, the value is now a method parameter reported by the browser.

The bean is session scoped: every HTTP session gets its own instance and singleton controllers receive a scoped proxy. The queue holds song ids only, never JPA entities, because entities would be detached and stale between requests. Public methods are synchronized because a browser can fire overlapping requests.

SRP: owns queue navigation and tracking rules; audio bytes are served by the media controller.

DIP: depends on SongRepository and PlaybackTrackingService abstractions.

Time Complexity: O(1) for all operations except setQueue(List) and playSong(Long, Double) (O(n) queue scan).

Space Complexity: O(n) where n = queue size.

  • Method Details

    • setQueue

      public void setQueue(List<Long> songIds)
      Replaces the queue with a shuffled copy of the given song ids and resets the position.

      Time Complexity: O(n). Space Complexity: O(n).

      Parameters:
      songIds - ids of the songs to queue

    • playSong

      public Song playSong(Long songId, Double position)
      Starts the given song: validates its file, applies the skip-tracking rule to the song being left, syncs the queue position and resets the tracking flags.
      Parameters:
      songId - id of the song to play
      position - seconds the previously playing song had reached, or null if unknown
      Returns:
      the song now current, with artists and album loaded
      Throws:
      NoSuchElementException - if the song does not exist, has no file path or its file is missing; the message is the desktop error text

    • playNext

      public Song playNext(Double position)
      Advances to the next queued song, wrapping around at the end.

      Does nothing when the queue is empty. The previous song is first passed through the "record on skip if at least 20 seconds" rule.

      Parameters:
      position - seconds the current song had reached, or null
      Returns:
      the new current song, or null when the queue is empty
      Throws:
      NoSuchElementException - if the next song cannot be played (see playSong(Long, Double))

    • playPrevious

      public MusicPlayerService.PreviousResult playPrevious(Double position)
      Goes to the previous queued song, or asks the browser to restart the current one.

      If the current song is more than 3 seconds in, nothing changes server side and MusicPlayerService.PreviousResult.restart() is true; the browser seeks to 0. Otherwise the queue moves back one position (wrapping) and that song starts.

      Parameters:
      position - seconds the current song had reached, or null
      Returns:
      the outcome; the song is null when the queue is empty
      Throws:
      NoSuchElementException - if the previous song cannot be played

    • markTracked

      public void markTracked()
      Records that the browser has played the current song for 20 seconds (the desktop 20 second timer).

      Creates the history row once per song; later calls for the same song do nothing.

    • songEnded

      public Song songEnded(int durationSeconds)
      Handles the natural end of the current song and moves on to the next one.

      Completes the history row with the full duration and marks it completed, then behaves like playNext(Double). With an empty queue playback stops.

      Parameters:
      durationSeconds - total length of the finished song as reported by the browser
      Returns:
      the next song, or null if the queue is empty
      Throws:
      NoSuchElementException - if the next song cannot be played
